d114SourceObservationDispositions.classification: Equivalent dimension convention, not a physical-direction defect
d114SourceObservationDispositions.sourcePixels: Both narrow Delta V intervals use exterior arrows approaching the vertical boundaries from outside.
d114SourceObservationDispositions.currentPixels: Both intervals use interior arrows pointing out to those same boundaries. The labels are below the arrow pairs rather than between exterior shafts.
d114SourceObservationDispositions.reason: Each pair is a two-ended interval marker, not a single gas-process or motion arrow. Both heads still identify the same two volume projections, both spans remain equal, and the current prose explicitly describes equal volume decreases starting at V1 and V2. Reversing the approach side does not reverse a compression process or change a measured span. Both pairs use the same convention and remain legible at 331px.

d114SourceObservationDispositions.classification: Equivalent short-span dimension convention; separate adjacent label defect remains
d114SourceObservationDispositions.sourcePixels: The short Delta p1 arrows approach the upper and lower levels from outside the bracket.
d114SourceObservationDispositions.currentPixels: Two nonzero arrowheads point from the midpoint toward those same two cap levels. Both heads are visible at full width and at 331px.
d114SourceObservationDispositions.reason: The opposed arrows delimit the pressure difference rather than specifying a time direction. The same upper/lower pressure levels, smaller-versus-larger comparison and index association are retained. The interval is short but still has two discernible end heads. The visible label/cap collision is independently failed as D117-READ-01; it is not evidence that changing the arrow convention itself changes the physics.

d114SourceObservationDispositions.classification: Equivalent offset dimension-cap convention, not a lost pressure correspondence
d114SourceObservationDispositions.sourcePixels: Pressure cap/guide strokes are continuous across the pressure axis.
d114SourceObservationDispositions.currentPixels: Each cap ends at x=90, and its matching guide starts at the pressure axis x=100. All four pairs stay horizontally aligned.
d114SourceObservationDispositions.reason: The repeated 10-construction-unit gap separates an external measurement annotation from the plot frame. At 331px it is about 5.17px wide; the correct same-level guide is still visually unambiguous. These are projection/measurement lines, not a physical pipe, wire or path whose continuity is instructional. No pressure level, curve crossing or interval endpoint is deleted. The cap touching the subscript is a separate readability failure.
